classification.difficultyReason: Sketch sine and its horizontal shift on shared axes, recognise the shifted curve as cosine, and express that relationship as an identity. The ordered drawing and comparison parts scaffold the connection.

answer.worked: Plot $(-\pi,0)$, $\left(-\frac{\pi}{2},-1\right)$, $(0,0)$, $\left(\frac{\pi}{2},1\right)$ and $(\pi,0)$. Join them with a smooth sine curve.

spec.sourceRegion: Challenge Problems, Problem 1(a), answer reference on teacher PDF page 47
spec.description: Sine curve on minus pi to pi, with half-pi ticks and y ticks at plus and minus one.

children.label: b
children.prompt: On the same set of axes, but in a different colour pen, sketch $y=\sin\left(x+\frac{\pi}{2}\right)$.

answer.short: The second curve shown in red.
answer.worked: Shift the sine curve $\frac{\pi}{2}$ to the left. On the same axes, plot $(-\pi,-1)$, $\left(-\frac{\pi}{2},0\right)$, $(0,1)$, $\left(\frac{\pi}{2},0\right)$ and $(\pi,-1)$, and join them smoothly in a different colour.

spec.sourceRegion: Challenge Problems, Problem 1(b), answer reference on teacher PDF page 47
spec.description: Blue sine and red shifted-sine curves on the same axes. Separate matching-colour equation captions sit below the graph.

children.label: c
children.prompt: What do you notice about your new curve?

answer.short: It is the graph of $y=\cos x$.
answer.worked: The new curve has maximum $(0,1)$, zeros at $x=\pm\frac{\pi}{2}$ and endpoint values $-1$ at $x=\pm\pi$. It coincides with $y=\cos x$.
